questions.question: Which of the following is **NOT** a Fundamental Duty?

options.text: To uphold and protect the unity and integrity of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To cast vote during elections**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Duties **

 
 
• The **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976)** modified the Constitution to include the **fundamental duties **of citizens.
 
• **Ten Fundamental Duties** were established in the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act**.
 
• **Part IVA, a new section, was added to the Constitution** as a result of this modification.
 
• This new section only has one article, **Article 51A**, which for the first time outlines a **list of the ten essential duties of citizens**.
 
• The **86th Amendment Act later added one additional Fundamental Duty**, which was added in **2002**. 
 
• **As per the Article 51A, some of the duties that are followed by every citizen include:**
 
 
• To protect the natural environment
 
• To abide by the Constitution
 
• To uphold and protect the unity and integrity of India
 
• To defend the country
 
• To promote harmony
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The fundamental duties can be used by the courts to determine **whether a law is constitutional**.
 
• The** Constitution of the former USSR** served as inspiration for the **Indian Constitution's Fundamental Duties**.
 
• **One of the most significant** constitutional amendments to India was the **42nd Amendment Act of 1976**.
 
• The **Indian National Congress**, led at the time by Indira Gandhi, **passed it**.
 
• The **Indian Constitution has undergone numerous revisions **as a result of this act, which is why it is often referred to as the **"Mini-Constitution."**
 
• **To cast vote during elections** is not a fundamental duty, it is a** constitutional right.**

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about mitochondria?

options.text: Mitochondria is present only in bacteria.
Mitochondria is present in all living cells.
Mitochondria is not bound by any membrane.
Mitochondria without outer membrane is called mitoplast.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Mitochondria without outer membrane is called mitoplast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mitochondria**__

 __
 
• All **eukaryotic cells have mitochondria**, which are **double membrane-bound organelles** that generate a**denosine triphosphate (ATP), the primary energy source required by the cell**.
 
• It is commonly known as the** "Powerhouse of the cell."**
 
• Both** plant and animal cells contain **the double-membraned, rod-shaped **mitochondria**.
 
• Its diameter varies from **0.5 to 1.0 micrometres**.
 
• The structure is made up of an **inner membrane, an outer membrane, cisternae, the intermembrane space and matrix**.
 
• The quantity of mitochondria **differs from cell to cell**.
 
• **RBC which is a type of living cell lacks mitochondria**, whereas liver cells have about 2000 per cell.
 
• In contrast to eukaryotes, **bacteria do not have membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria** or chloroplasts.
 
• Mitochondria without an **outer membrane are called mitoplast**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The mitochondria also perform **signaling, cellular differentiation, cell death, and maintenance of cell cycle growth**.
 
• Mitochondria have their **own genetic material**.
 
• The i**ntermembrane space serves as a barrier between the layers of proteins and phospholipids that make up the outer membrane and the inner membrane**.
 
• The mitochondrion's **outer membrane** is made up of** numerous unique proteins called porins and covers its surface**. 
 
• The** genome of human mitochondria** is **circular DNA**.

questions.question: Which type of radiation designates a part of the electromagnetic spectrum with frequencies approximately from 300 GHz to 3 kHz, or equivalent, wavelengths approximately from 1 mm to 100 km?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radio waves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Radio waves**

 
 
• In the electromagnetic spectrum,** radio waves have wavelengths that are longer than those of infrared light**.
 
• They have **wavelengths** that range from **1 millimetre to 100 kilometres**, and **frequencies** that range from **300 GHz to as low as 3 kHz**.
 
• **Radio waves move at the speed of light**, just like all other electromagnetic waves.
 
• **Lightning and celestial objects **are the two main **sources of naturally produced radio waves**.
 
• **Fixed and mobile radio communication, broadcasting, radar, and other navigation systems, communications satellites, computer networks, and countless more applications** all require **artificially produced radio waves**.
 
• In the** Earth's atmosphere**, different radio wave frequencies **propagate in different ways**.
 
• **Shorter waves** can travel** around the world** and reflect off the ionosphere, while **much shorter wavelengths bend or reflect very little** and move along a **line of sight**.
 
• **Long waves** may cover a **portion of the Earth** quite consistently.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The current in the bulb will stop flowing:

options.text: when the switch is turned on

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**if the circuit is broken**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electric Current**__

 __
 
• A **stream of charged particles, such as electrons (negative charge) or ions, travelling through an electrical conductor or a vacuum** is known as an electric current. 
 
• **Charge carriers are the moving particles** that, depending on the conductor, can be of different types of particles.
 
• In** motors, generators, inductors, and transformers, magnetic fields **produced by electric currents are employed. 
 
• Electric current travels from a **cell's positive electrode to its negative electrode, or from a cell's high potential to its low potential**.
 
• Only when a **circuit is complete or in a form of a closed loop, the flow of current is seen**.
 
• The** flow of current in a bulb or any conductor** will stop if **there is any breakage in the circuit**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Positive and negative terminals **are regarded as having** high and low potential**, respectively.
 
• Although** negative charge always moves from low potential to high potential**, **positive charge always moves from high potential to low potential**. 
 
• So, we can say that the **direction of current is always opposite to the direction of flow of electron **is low potential to high potential.
 
• A **power source, like a battery**, is required for a circuit, and** current must flow through a conductor, like a wire**.
 
• Components like** bulbs, buzzers, and motors** convert **power into light**, sound, and motion.

questions.question: NDP at FC = GDP at FC minus _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**depreciation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NDP at FC**

 
 
• The **revenue **that the factors receive in the form of **wages, profits, rent, interest**, etc. is known as the **Net Domestic Product at Factor Cost (NDP at FC)**. 
 
 
 
• **GDP**
 
 
• The **total value added in a particular economy** is measured by the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**.
 
• The value-added, sometimes referred to as **intermediate consumption**, **is the difference between the price of the goods and services produced and the price of the goods and services required to produce them**.
 
 
 
• Formula to **calculate NDP FC**
 
 
• It is computed by **deducting depreciation from the gross domestic product (GDP)** and it is represented as;
 
 

** NDP at FC = GDP at FC - depreciation**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One of the primary indicators of economic growth that the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reports on a quarterly basis is NDP, along with GDP, gross national income (GNI), gross domestic product (GNP), and disposable income, and personal income. 
 
• Components of NDP are** NDP at Factor Cost = NDP as Market Price-Indirect Cases+Subsidies**.
 
• **Gross National Product (GNP)**, which is determined without depreciation or the consumption of capital utilized in the manufacturing process, **is the total market value of the final goods and services produced by a country's economy during a specified time period **(usually a year).
 
• **Gross National Income (GNI) is the entire amount of money a nation receives from its citizens and enterprises**, whether they are located in the country or abroad.

questions.question: The Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2021 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 15 March 2021, which amended the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1957**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957** regulates the mining sector in India.
 
• The amendment proposes to allow captive miners of both coal and other minerals to sell up to** 50 percent** of their production after meeting the requirements of the end-use plant and paying additional royalty to the state government. 
 
• Operators are currently only allowed to use **coal and minerals **extracted from captive mines for their own industrial use. 
 
• This increased flexibility would allow miners to **maximize output** from captive mines as they would be able to sell output in excess of their own requirements.
 
• The amendment also proposes to** fix additional royalty payments to states** for the extension of mining leases for central public sector enterprises.
 
• Another key change the Bill proposes is to **empower the central government to conduct auctions or re-auction processes** for the grant of a mining lease if a state government fails to complete the auction process in a specified period, decided after consultations between the Centre and state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Ministry of Mines, a branch of the Government of India, functions as the primary body for the **formulation and administration of laws relating to mines in India**. 
 
• The head of the ministry is **Pralhad Joshi**, who has been serving since June 2019.

questions.question: Why do people living in the Konkan coast NOT encounter extremes of temperature and seasonal rhythm?

options.text: Location on leeward side of Sahyadri

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coastal Location**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• With a long **coastline**, large coastal areas have an equable climate. 
 
• Areas in the interior of India are far away from the moderating influence of the sea. 
 
• Such areas have extremes of climate.
 
• That is why the people of **Mumbai** and the **Konkan** coast have hardly any idea of extremes of temperature and the seasonal rhythm of weather.
 
• India‘s climate is controlled by a number of factors which can be broadly divided into **two groups** — factors related to location and relief, and factors related to air pressure and winds. 
 
• Factors related to Location and Relief Latitude: the **Tropic of Cancer** passes through the central part of India in an east-west direction. 
 
• Thus, the northern part of India lies in a **sub-tropical **and** temperate zone** and the part lying south of the Tropic of Cancer falls in the tropical zone. 
 
• The tropical zone being **nearer** to the equator experiences high temperatures throughout the year with a small daily and annual range. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Undulating landform** means to have a continuous up and down shape or movement, like waves on the sea.
 
• The **leeward side** is the drier side or the side where the trade winds pass after they hit a mountain.
 
• **Nagpur** lies in interior Maharashtra on the leeward side of the Sahyadri Mountains.
 
• A **monsoon** is a seasonal change in the direction of the prevailing, or strongest, winds of a region.
 
• Monsoons cause wet and dry seasons throughout much of the tropics.
 
• Monsoons are most often associated with the Indian Ocean.
 
• Monsoons always blow from cold to warm regions.

questions.question: Name the classical dancer who was awarded the ‘Sangeet Natak Akademi Award’ in 1966 for his contribution to Odissi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kelucharan Mohapatra.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kelucharan Mohapatra** was a great teacher and is still alive in the hearts of the people who pursue and admire the Indian Classical dance of Odisha.
 
• **Kelucharan Mohapatra** is the proud winner of many precious awards. 
 
• He won **Padma Shri Award** in the year 1972 and the **Sangeet Natak Academy Award **in 1966. 
 
• In 1989, he became the proud winner of the **Padma Bhushan Award**. 
 
• He was honoured with the **Sangeet Academy Fellowship** in 1991. 
 
• Again, in the year 2000, he was awarded the highly remarkable **Padma Vibhushan Award.** 
 
• The government of Madhya Pradesh honoured him with the **Kalidas Samman** too.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nileshwar Mukherjee, Bipin Singh, and Haricharan Singh** were famous Manipuri dancer.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Academy recognizes eight – **Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Kathakali, Sattriya, Manipuri, and Mohiniyattam**. 
 
• 
 
 
 Sangeet Natak Akademi – India’s national academy of music, dance, and drama – is the first national academy of the arts set up by the Republic of India. It was created by a resolution of the (then) Ministry of Education, Government of India, dated** 31 May 1952**, which was notified in the Gazette of India of June** 1952**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the Sahitya Akademi Award winning novel of the Indian writer Amitav Ghosh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Shadow Lines**__.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****

__
 
• Amitav Ghosh was awarded the **Sahitya Akademi Award in 1990** for his book **The Shadow Lines** and the **Padma Shri in 2007 **for his services to literature and education. 
 
• His first novel, **The Circle of Reason** (1986), follows an Indian protagonist who, suspected of being a terrorist, leaves India for northern Africa and the Middle East.
 
• Author **Amitav Ghosh** was felicitated with the** 54th Jnanpith Award** for his “**outstanding contribution to the enrichment of Indian Literature in English**”.
 
• Mr. Ghosh who is a social anthropologist by academic training has written extensively in both fiction and non-fiction sphere of literature. His works has been translated in more than **30 languages**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sahitya Akademi Award,** also known as **Sahitya Akademi Main Award,** is conferred on **24 writers in 24 languages** annually for the most outstanding books of literary merit published in any of the major Indian languages recognized by the Akademi.
 
• The award amount, which was Rs.5,000 since inception, had been enhanced to Rs.10,000 from 1983, Rs.25,000 from 1988, Rs.40,000 from 2001, Rs.50,000 from 2003 and is now **Rs.1,00,000** from 2009. The first Awards were given in **1955.**
 
• Besides the 22 languages enumerated in the Constitution of India, the Sahitya Akademi has recognised **English and Rajasthani **as languages in which its programme may be implemented
 
• The Head Office of the Sahitya Akademi is housed in** Rabindra Bhavan, 35 Ferozeshah Road, New Delhi.**

questions.question: The Sangeet Natak Akademi was set up in the year _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1953.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi**

 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi,** the apex body in the field of performing arts in the country, was **formed in ****1953.**
 
• It was **set up for the preservation and promotion of the vast intangible heritage of India's diverse culture expressed in forms of music, dance, and drama.**
 
• The management of the Akademi vests in its **General Council.**
 
• **Ariyakudi Ramanuja Iyengar Karaikudi **was the first to receive the **Sahitya Natak Akademi award.**
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Puraskar** is an award given by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi,** **India's National Academy of Music, Dance & Drama.**
 
• The **Sangeet Natak Academy **was **established on 31 May 1952** by a resolution of the Ministry of Human Resource development.
 
• The Akademi was officially **inaugurated on 28 January 1953** **by the first President of India Rajendra Prasad ****and**** **PV Rajmannar **was appointed as its first Chairman.**
